detail.longDescription: We have GitHub rulesets to prohibit pushes to our primary branches ( dev and main ) by way of "Restrict updates". Then, we have the same ruleset enforcing "Require a pull request before merging". This is good. The trouble is that the PR cannot merge to dev or main unless I either: Use the bypass button Turn off "Restrict updates" The bypass button is a lousy option because it bypasses not just the "Restrict updates" protection. If I turn off "Restrict updates" then somehow people can push straight to dev anyway, despite "Require a pull request before merging" being on. Bypass list only includes "Allow for pull requests only" which I don't like. So I end up having to turn on and off "Restrict updates" all the time to allow PRs. Is there a better way? Recreation procedure: Branch off dev , a protected branch. Say your branch name is feat/hello Do some things on feat/hello PR back to dev . Merging is blocked because "Restrict updates" is active for dev. Goal: Prohibit direct pushes to dev Only allow PRs to merge to dev Avoid having to turn on and off "Restrict updates" all the time
